title: Her uncle's band in Homestead and her first taste of show business
summary: Her uncle Harry led a band in Homestead that recorded on Gennett and let her sing; through him she got a first job.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: But Harry didn't like being on the road, so he came back to Homestead. And he also didn't like to play the drums. He wanted to play the sax. So he began -- he formed a group called "The Red Hot Peppers." And this --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
the band, you know, and he let me sing every once-in-a-while.
In fact, that was actually my first let's say, taste of show business. I hadn't considered singing as a career.
But naturally, by this being my uncle and he having a band, I used to tag along with the band, and he let me sing.
It was through my uncle and a friend of his that I got my first job in Pittsburgh working at the Benjamin Harrison Literary Club in 1936.
But this particular album was made --
You know, we just showed up there, just the two of us. And I had brought some music, but he knew all the songs.
